title: Activepieces Tutorial for Building Your First Workflow
summary: Activepieces tutorial explains how to connect apps with automated workflows. Set up your first automation using 744+ integrations.
body_markdown:
## Build your first workflow in six stages


Build the flow in six stages, each ending with something that works, so that if you stop at any point you've a tested integration rather than a half-wired draft.


### Stage 1: Create the workflow and name it


Sign up on the free cloud plan at cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up, then create a new workflow from the Flows page. A run costs 1 credit however many steps it has, so the free allowance goes a long way while you test.


Rename it immediately to say what it does, such as "Weekly site audit", because default names turn a list of flows into a guessing game once a second person starts building.


### Stage 2: Add a trigger and test it


Click the trigger slot on the canvas and choose one. A schedule trigger is the safest first choice, since it needs no outside account.


In the settings panel that opens, set the day, hour and timezone. Then use the sample-data option to load an example payload.


Every step carries its own test button, so you prove each one before adding the next. Once the trigger returns sample data, you have something real to map in Stage 4.


### Stage 3: Add an action and connect an account


Click the plus beneath the trigger and pick one action, from an app you already use, such as a document or messaging tool. When prompted, create the connection by signing in to that app and granting access.


Where your organisation allows it, use a dedicated or shared service account, because a connection tied to one person's login stops working when that person leaves.


### Stage 4: Map data from the trigger into the action


Open the action's input fields and click into one. The data selector lists the output of earlier steps; choose the field you want rather than typing it.


Map one field only on this first pass. A single working mapping is easier to debug than five separate ones.


### Stage 5: Test, then publish


Press the test button on the action and check the destination app itself for the result. Only when it appears there should you publish, using the button at the top that warns of unpublished changes.


**Until you publish, the flow won't run on its own** , which is a common first-week surprise for new builders.


### Stage 6: Read the Runs page


Open Runs to see each execution with its status and, inside it, the input and output of every step. When something fails, this is where you find which step broke and what it received.


With the first flow now live you can decide on evidence whether to stay on cloud, self-host or move to a paid plan.


The next flow doesn't need a builder at all. Open the built-in chat in Activepieces, describe a process that touches your connected apps, and it publishes a live flow in your account, the same artifact you just assembled by hand.


That flow runs under the same RBAC and audit logs as every human-built one, and its run trace shows exactly what happened, readable by anyone without a certification. You don't hire for this; you describe it. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


> You don't hire for this; you describe it.
